authored.prompt: In this lab a PUT or DELETE with no precondition header is answered with 428 before the store is touched. Which line produces that response?
authored.explanation: ExpectedVersion returns `Results.StatusCode(428)` when If-Match is absent (02-CONCEPTS.md:10-12).

authored.prompt: Compare-and-change: the version comparison must run inside the same lock as the assignment so only one of two writers with the same tag can advance the item. Which line is that comparison?
authored.explanation: TaskStore.Replace holds `lock (gate)` while it finds, compares, constructs and stores (02-CONCEPTS.md:17-22); Program.cs:32 only translates the Conflict outcome into 412.

authored.prompt: A blank or oversized title is rejected before the store mutates anything, and trimming happens before the length rule. Where is that rule evaluated?
authored.explanation: `Valid` checks `input.Title?.Trim().Length is >= 1 and <= 120`; TaskStore.Create trims but assumes already-validated input (02-CONCEPTS.md:24-28; 06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md:26-28).

authored.prompt: After a successful replace, the response tag must come from the record this mutation returned, not from a re-read that could see a later writer. Which line sets it?
authored.explanation: The PUT handler sets `ETag = Tag(item!.Version)` from the store's returned record (07-TRACE-LAB.md:19-21).

authored.prompt: The concurrent-replace check must assert the one-winner property without depending on which request the scheduler lets in first. Which line asserts it?
authored.explanation: HttpChecks asserts exactly one 200 and one 412 (and a winner of A or B at version 2), not a particular winner (07-TRACE-LAB.md:26-28).

authored.prompt: Goal: state the lab's contract for a PUT whose If-Match is a well-formed quoted number that is no longer current. Which response verifies it?

choices.text: 400 Bad Request with the ETag-syntax error
409 Conflict, and the stored task keeps its current version

authored.explanation: Missing preconditions return 428, malformed tag syntax 400, and a valid but outdated version 412 (02-CONCEPTS.md:10-12).

authored.prompt: Goal: decide whether TaskStore's one-winner guarantee survives running two application instances. Which conclusion is the verified one?

choices.text: yes: `lock (gate)` serialises every writer on the machine, so a request arriving at the second instance simply waits for the first one to release it
no: each instance has its own lock and dictionary, so the database operation itself must carry the expected version and handle no matching row
yes, as long as both instances read the ETag before writing

authored.explanation: A process-local lock is not a distributed concurrency mechanism (02-CONCEPTS.md:30-35).

authored.prompt: Goal: trace a PUT with a blank title but the correct If-Match tag. Which observation verifies your trace?

choices.text: 412, because the tag is checked after the title
400 returned before the store runs; the version is not consumed
200 and version plus one; the stored title stays as it was before the PUT

authored.explanation: An invalid title returns before the mutation operation, so it does not consume a version (07-TRACE-LAB.md:30-31; Program.cs:27).

authored.prompt: Goal: design the database replace as `UPDATE ... WHERE id = @id AND version = @expected`. What must your answer say about the affected-row count?

choices.text: one row means the conditional mutation succeeded; zero rows needs an explicit missing-versus-conflict policy, and any follow-up read has its own timing limits
zero rows always means the version was stale, so return 412; a missing task would already have failed the earlier read, so no follow-up read is needed
zero rows always means the task does not exist, so return 404
retry the UPDATE with the newest version until one row is affected
